cdus.topic: Metformin Titration & Safety in Renal Impairment
cdus.entry_criteria: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73m2
mandated_actions: Cap Metformin at 1000mg/day (500mg BD) if eGFR 30-44 mL/min
Monitor eGFR every 3-6 months
Add SGLT2 inhibitor for dual cardio-renal and glycemic benefit if eGFR >=20
negative_boundaries: 🛑 NEVER prescribe full-dose Metformin (>1000mg/day) when eGFR is <45 mL/min.
🛑 Stop Metformin completely if eGFR falls <30 mL/min or during acute dehydrating illness.
cdus.verbatim_excerpt: Metformin is safe when eGFR is >=45. When eGFR is 30-44 mL/min, maximum recommended dose is 1000 mg daily (500 mg twice daily). Metformin is contraindicated if eGFR is <30 mL/min due to risk of lactic acidosis.
danger_signs: Nausea, vomiting, lethargy, severe metabolic acidosis
cdus.prompt_injection_chunk:
[CDU-T2D-METFORMIN-RENAL]
CONDITION: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73m2
GUIDELINE ACTIONS: Cap Metformin at 1000mg/day (500mg BD) if eGFR 30-44 mL/min Monitor eGFR every 3-6 months Add SGLT2 inhibitor for dual cardio-renal and glycemic benefit if eGFR >=20
NEGATIVE BOUNDARIES: 🛑 NEVER prescribe full-dose Metformin (>1000mg/day) when eGFR is <45 mL/min. 🛑 Stop Metformin completely if eGFR falls <30 mL/min or during acute dehydrating illness.

cdus.topic: HFrEF Guideline Directed Medical Therapy (GDMT) Initiation
cdus.source_guideline: ESC 2023 Guidelines for Heart Failure / AHA-ACC-HFSA 2022
cdus.entry_criteria: HFrEF (LVEF <= 40%) with NYHA Class II-IV symptoms
mandated_actions: Initiate SGLT2 inhibitor (Dapagliflozin 10mg or Empagliflozin 10mg OD)
Evaluate MRA initiation (Spironolactone 12.5-25mg OD) only after verifying baseline K+ < 5.0
negative_boundaries: 🛑 DO NOT initiate Spironolactone if baseline K+ >= 5.0 mmol/L or eGFR <30 mL/min.
🛑 Baseline K+ 4.9 requires immediate recheck within 1-2 weeks before MRA initiation.
cdus.verbatim_excerpt: SGLT2 inhibitors are recommended for all patients with HFrEF to reduce heart failure hospitalization and cardiovascular death. Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (Spironolactone/Eplerenone) are recommended for all symptomatic HFrEF, provided potassium is <5.0 and eGFR >30.
cdus.prompt_injection_chunk:
[CDU-HF-SGLT2I-MRA]
CONDITION: HFrEF (LVEF <= 40%) with NYHA Class II-IV symptoms
GUIDELINE ACTIONS: Initiate SGLT2 inhibitor (Dapagliflozin 10mg or Empagliflozin 10mg OD) Evaluate MRA initiation (Spironolactone 12.5-25mg OD) only after verifying baseline K+ < 5.0
NEGATIVE BOUNDARIES: 🛑 DO NOT initiate Spironolactone if baseline K+ >= 5.0 mmol/L or eGFR <30 mL/min. 🛑 Baseline K+ 4.9 requires immediate recheck within 1-2 weeks before MRA initiation.

cdus.source_guideline: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for CKD
cdus.entry_criteria: CKD Stage 3 or higher receiving RAAS inhibitor therapy
mandated_actions: Monitor serum potassium and creatinine within 1-2 weeks of initiating or titrating RAASi/MRA
Educate patient on dietary potassium sources
negative_boundaries: 🛑 DO NOT combine dual RAAS blockade (ACEi + ARB) due to acute kidney injury and hyperkalemia hazard.
🛑 Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-based salt substitutes.
cdus.verbatim_excerpt: Serum potassium should be monitored regularly in patients receiving renin-angiotensin system inhibitors or mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists. Dual RAAS blockade is contraindicated.
cdus.prompt_injection_chunk:
[CDU-CKD-POTASSIUM-SAFETY]
CONDITION: CKD Stage 3 or higher receiving RAAS inhibitor therapy
GUIDELINE ACTIONS: Monitor serum potassium and creatinine within 1-2 weeks of initiating or titrating RAASi/MRA Educate patient on dietary potassium sources
NEGATIVE BOUNDARIES: 🛑 DO NOT combine dual RAAS blockade (ACEi + ARB) due to acute kidney injury and hyperkalemia hazard. 🛑 Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-based salt substitutes.

cdus.topic: Acute Gout Management in High-Risk Multi-Morbidity
cdus.source_guideline: ACR 2020 Guideline for the Management of Gout / NICE NG219
cdus.entry_criteria: Acute gout flare in patient with underlying CKD or cardiovascular disease
mandated_actions: Prescribe short-course oral Prednisolone (20-30mg daily for 3-5 days) or intra-articular steroid
Maintain existing maintenance Allopurinol without alteration during the acute flare
negative_boundaries: 🛑 STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATE oral/systemic NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Naproxen, Diclofenac, Indomethacin, Celecoxib) due to severe risk of acute-on-chronic renal failure and heart failure decompensation.
🛑 Avoid full-dose Colchicine (severe neuro/myopathy risk in eGFR <35).
cdus.verbatim_excerpt: Oral glucocorticoids are first-line for acute gout in patients with renal impairment or heart failure. Systemic NSAIDs should be avoided in severe CKD and heart failure. Do not alter maintenance allopurinol during an acute flare.
danger_signs: Severe pain, joint warmth, refusal to bear weight
Risk of NSAID-induced acute renal failure
cdus.prompt_injection_chunk:
[CDU-GOUT-ACUTE-FLARE]
CONDITION: Acute gout flare in patient with underlying CKD or cardiovascular disease
GUIDELINE ACTIONS: Prescribe short-course oral Prednisolone (20-30mg daily for 3-5 days) or intra-articular steroid Maintain existing maintenance Allopurinol without alteration during the acute flare
NEGATIVE BOUNDARIES: 🛑 STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATE oral/systemic NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Naproxen, Diclofenac, Indomethacin, Celecoxib) due to severe risk of acute-on-chronic renal failure and heart failure decompensation. 🛑 Avoid full-dose Colchicine (severe neuro/myopathy risk in eGFR <35).

cdus.topic: Bronchospasm Risk & Beta-Blocker Prohibitions in Asthma
cdus.source_guideline: GINA 2024 Global Strategy for Asthma Management and Prevention
cdus.entry_criteria: Active asthma or history of reactive airway disease requiring cardiac therapy
mandated_actions: Maintain inhaled corticosteroid controller therapy
Select non-beta-blocker alternatives (e.g. Calcium Channel Blockers, Nitrates) for angina and hypertension
negative_boundaries: 🛑 STRICTLY PROHIBIT non-selective beta-blockers (Propranolol, Carvedilol, Labetalol, Timolol eye drops). Non-selective beta-blockade precipitates severe bronchospasm and fatal status asthmaticus.
🛑 Avoid non-cardioselective beta-blockade even if cardioselective alternatives exist unless no other anti-anginal is viable.
cdus.verbatim_excerpt: Non-selective beta-blockers (oral or ophthalmic) are contraindicated in asthma as they can cause severe, life-threatening bronchospasm. Cardioselective beta-blockers should be used with extreme caution only when no alternative exists.
danger_signs: Wheezing, chest tightness, drop in peak expiratory flow
cdus.prompt_injection_chunk:
[CDU-ASTHMA-DRUG-SAFETY]
CONDITION: Active asthma or history of reactive airway disease requiring cardiac therapy
GUIDELINE ACTIONS: Maintain inhaled corticosteroid controller therapy Select non-beta-blocker alternatives (e.g. Calcium Channel Blockers, Nitrates) for angina and hypertension
NEGATIVE BOUNDARIES: 🛑 STRICTLY PROHIBIT non-selective beta-blockers (Propranolol, Carvedilol, Labetalol, Timolol eye drops). Non-selective beta-blockade precipitates severe bronchospasm and fatal status asthmaticus. 🛑 Avoid non-cardioselective beta-blockade even if cardioselective alternatives exist unless no other anti-anginal is viable.

cdus.topic: Stable Ischemic Heart Disease / Angina in Asthma
cdus.source_guideline: NICE CG126 / AHA-ACC Chronic Coronary Disease 2023
cdus.entry_criteria: Stable exertional angina with beta-blocker contraindication
mandated_actions: Initiate Dihydropyridine CCB (Amlodipine 5-10mg OD)
Prescribe Sublingual Nitroglycerin PRN for acute attacks
Arrange outpatient cardiac referral/investigation
negative_boundaries: 🛑 NEVER initiate non-selective beta-blocker in patient with active asthma.
cdus.verbatim_excerpt: When beta-blockers are contraindicated in patients with asthma, calcium channel blockers (dihydropyridine or non-dihydropyridine) are recommended as first-line anti-anginal therapy.
cdus.prompt_injection_chunk:
[CDU-ANGINA-FIRSTLINE]
CONDITION: Stable exertional angina with beta-blocker contraindication
GUIDELINE ACTIONS: Initiate Dihydropyridine CCB (Amlodipine 5-10mg OD) Prescribe Sublingual Nitroglycerin PRN for acute attacks Arrange outpatient cardiac referral/investigation
NEGATIVE BOUNDARIES: 🛑 NEVER initiate non-selective beta-blocker in patient with active asthma.

cdus.topic: Secondary Upper GI Bleed Prevention in Anticoagulation
cdus.source_guideline: ACG-CAG 2022 Management of Anticoagulants in GI Bleeding
cdus.entry_criteria: Oral anticoagulation with documented history of peptic ulcer hemorrhage
mandated_actions: Maintain continuous Proton Pump Inhibitor (Pantoprazole 40mg OD)
Strictly avoid systemic NSAID co-prescription
negative_boundaries: 🛑 STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATE oral non-selective NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Naproxen, Diclofenac) and high-dose Aspirin. Concurrent NSAID + DOAC increases fatal upper GI rebleeding hazard by 4- to 6-fold.
🛑 DO NOT stop life-saving anticoagulation for minor musculoskeletal pain.
cdus.verbatim_excerpt: Patients requiring oral anticoagulation after a healed peptic ulcer bleed must receive co-prescribed daily proton pump inhibitor therapy. Concomitant systemic NSAIDs are contraindicated as they increase bleeding risk by over 400%.
danger_signs: Melena, hematemesis, orthostatic drop in blood pressure
cdus.prompt_injection_chunk:
[CDU-PUD-BLEEDING-SAFETY]
CONDITION: Oral anticoagulation with documented history of peptic ulcer hemorrhage
GUIDELINE ACTIONS: Maintain continuous Proton Pump Inhibitor (Pantoprazole 40mg OD) Strictly avoid systemic NSAID co-prescription
NEGATIVE BOUNDARIES: 🛑 STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATE oral non-selective NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Naproxen, Diclofenac) and high-dose Aspirin. Concurrent NSAID + DOAC increases fatal upper GI rebleeding hazard by 4- to 6-fold. 🛑 DO NOT stop life-saving anticoagulation for minor musculoskeletal pain.

cdus.topic: Safe Osteoarthritis Analgesia in High Bleeding Risk
cdus.entry_criteria: Knee osteoarthritis in patients with gastrointestinal bleeding risk
mandated_actions: Prescribe Topical Diclofenac 1% gel (localized application)
Recommend regular scheduled Paracetamol up to 3g/day
Offer intra-articular corticosteroid knee injection for severe flares
negative_boundaries: 🛑 NEVER prescribe systemic oral NSAIDs or COX-2 inhibitors to patients on oral anticoagulation with recent peptic ulcer.
cdus.verbatim_excerpt: Topical NSAIDs are strongly recommended for knee osteoarthritis and have substantially lower systemic gastrointestinal and renal adverse effects than oral NSAIDs. Intra-articular corticosteroids provide effective short-term relief without bleeding risk.
cdus.prompt_injection_chunk:
[CDU-OA-ANALGESIA]
CONDITION: Knee osteoarthritis in patients with gastrointestinal bleeding risk
GUIDELINE ACTIONS: Prescribe Topical Diclofenac 1% gel (localized application) Recommend regular scheduled Paracetamol up to 3g/day Offer intra-articular corticosteroid knee injection for severe flares
NEGATIVE BOUNDARIES: 🛑 NEVER prescribe systemic oral NSAIDs or COX-2 inhibitors to patients on oral anticoagulation with recent peptic ulcer.

cdus.topic: Deprescribing Sulfonylureas & Relaxing Glycemic Targets in Frail Elderly
cdus.source_guideline: ADA Standards of Care 2024 (Older Adults) / STOPP-START Criteria v3
cdus.entry_criteria: Type 2 Diabetes in patient >= 75 years with frailty, dementia, or fall risk
mandated_actions: Deprescribe long-acting sulfonylureas (Glibenclamide)
Target relaxed HbA1c of 7.5% - 8.0%
Substitute with safer agent (e.g. Linagliptin) or lifestyle if glucose acceptable
negative_boundaries: 🛑 STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATE Glibenclamide in elderly patients (Beers Criteria / STOPP violation; prolonged renal excretion causes catastrophic prolonged hypoglycemia).
🛑 NEVER aim for tight glycemic control (HbA1c < 7.0%) in frail fall-prone elderly.
cdus.verbatim_excerpt: In frail older adults with multiple chronic illnesses, extensive comorbidity, or history of falls, HbA1c target should be relaxed to 7.5%-8.5%. Long-acting sulfonylureas (Glibenclamide) should be avoided due to the high risk of severe and prolonged hypoglycemia.
cdus.prompt_injection_chunk:
[CDU-FRAIL-T2D-TARGETS]
CONDITION: Type 2 Diabetes in patient >= 75 years with frailty, dementia, or fall risk
GUIDELINE ACTIONS: Deprescribe long-acting sulfonylureas (Glibenclamide) Target relaxed HbA1c of 7.5% - 8.0% Substitute with safer agent (e.g. Linagliptin) or lifestyle if glucose acceptable
NEGATIVE BOUNDARIES: 🛑 STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATE Glibenclamide in elderly patients (Beers Criteria / STOPP violation; prolonged renal excretion causes catastrophic prolonged hypoglycemia). 🛑 NEVER aim for tight glycemic control (HbA1c < 7.0%) in frail fall-prone elderly.

cdus.topic: Pharmacotherapy Safety & NSAID Prohibitions in Cirrhosis
cdus.source_guideline: EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines: Management of Decompensated Cirrhosis 2023
mandated_actions: Audit all prescribed and OTC medications for hepatotoxicity and renal risk
Monitor renal function during any acute illness or infection
negative_boundaries: 🛑 ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION to oral or parenteral NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Naproxen, Diclofenac). NSAIDs trigger irreversible hepatorenal syndrome and lethal variceal bleeding.
🛑 AVOID sedating opioids (Morphine, Oxycodone, Codeine) which precipitate acute hepatic encephalopathy.
cdus.verbatim_excerpt: NSAIDs are absolutely contraindicated in patients with cirrhosis as they inhibit renal prostaglandins, precipitating acute renal failure (hepatorenal syndrome) and gastrointestinal bleeding. Sedating opioids should be avoided as they trigger hepatic encephalopathy.
danger_signs: Oliguria, rise in creatinine, jaundice, asterixis, confusion
cdus.prompt_injection_chunk:
[CDU-CIRRHOSIS-MED-SAFETY]
CONDITION: Compensated or decompensated liver cirrhosis
GUIDELINE ACTIONS: Audit all prescribed and OTC medications for hepatotoxicity and renal risk Monitor renal function during any acute illness or infection
NEGATIVE BOUNDARIES: 🛑 ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION to oral or parenteral NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Naproxen, Diclofenac). NSAIDs trigger irreversible hepatorenal syndrome and lethal variceal bleeding. 🛑 AVOID sedating opioids (Morphine, Oxycodone, Codeine) which precipitate acute hepatic encephalopathy.

cdus.source_guideline: AASLD Practice Guidance 2022 / British Journal of Anaesthesia 2022
cdus.entry_criteria: Acute or chronic pain in patient with liver cirrhosis
mandated_actions: Cap Paracetamol at a strict maximum of 2.0g per 24 hours (500mg QDS or 1000mg BD)
negative_boundaries: 🛑 NEVER exceed Paracetamol 2.0g/day in cirrhosis.
🛑 NEVER give NSAIDs.
cdus.verbatim_excerpt: Paracetamol is the safest first-line analgesic in cirrhosis, provided dose is strictly restricted to a maximum of 2.0g per 24 hours.
cdus.prompt_injection_chunk:
[CDU-CIRRHOSIS-ANALGESIA]
CONDITION: Acute or chronic pain in patient with liver cirrhosis
GUIDELINE ACTIONS: Cap Paracetamol at a strict maximum of 2.0g per 24 hours (500mg QDS or 1000mg BD)
NEGATIVE BOUNDARIES: 🛑 NEVER exceed Paracetamol 2.0g/day in cirrhosis. 🛑 NEVER give NSAIDs.

cdus.topic: Triptan Vascular Contraindications in Severe Hypertension
cdus.source_guideline: AHS Guidelines for Acute Migraine 2024 / BNF Triptan Precautions
cdus.entry_criteria: Migraine headache in patient with blood pressure >= 160/100 mmHg
mandated_actions: Withhold Triptans until blood pressure is lowered < 140/90 mmHg
Provide non-vasoconstrictive abortive therapy (Paracetamol, Metoclopramide) for acute migraine
negative_boundaries: 🛑 ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION to Triptans (Sumatriptan, Zolmitriptan) in uncontrolled Stage 2 hypertension (BP >=160/100). Triptans cause coronary and cerebral vasoconstriction, carrying high risk of ischemic stroke and myocardial infarction.
cdus.verbatim_excerpt: Triptans are 5-HT1B/1D receptor agonists that induce cerebral and coronary vasoconstriction. They are strictly contraindicated in uncontrolled moderate-to-severe hypertension (systolic BP >=160 mmHg or diastolic BP >=100 mmHg) due to increased risk of ischemic stroke and acute coronary syndromes.
danger_signs: Chest pain during or after triptan intake
cdus.prompt_injection_chunk:
[CDU-TRIPTAN-VASCULAR-SAFETY]
CONDITION: Migraine headache in patient with blood pressure >= 160/100 mmHg
GUIDELINE ACTIONS: Withhold Triptans until blood pressure is lowered < 140/90 mmHg Provide non-vasoconstrictive abortive therapy (Paracetamol, Metoclopramide) for acute migraine

cdus.topic: Fatal D2 Antagonist Prohibitions in Parkinson's Disease
cdus.source_guideline: NICE NG71 (Parkinson's Disease) / Movement Disorder Society 2023
cdus.entry_criteria: Parkinson's Disease presenting with hallucinations, agitation, or delirium
mandated_actions: Screen for underlying delirium causes (infections, metabolic)
If antipsychotic necessary, permit ONLY Quetiapine (12.5-25mg) or Clozapine / Pimavanserin
negative_boundaries: 🛑 ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION to First-Generation Antipsychotics (Haloperidol) and D2-blocking Second-Generation Antipsychotics (Risperidone, Olanzapine, Aripiprazole) -> Catastrophic motor collapse/death.
🛑 STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATE D2-blocking antiemetics (Metoclopramide, Prochlorperazine).
cdus.verbatim_excerpt: Typical antipsychotics (e.g. haloperidol) and most atypical antipsychotics (e.g. risperidone, olanzapine) block dopamine D2 receptors and cause severe, irreversible worsening of parkinsonism. Only quetiapine, pimavanserin, or clozapine are safe.
danger_signs: Severe rigidity, inability to swallow, acute motor arrest

cdus.topic: Tricyclic Antidepressant Prohibitions in Severe BPH
cdus.source_guideline: EAU Guidelines on Management of Non-neurogenic Male LUTS 2024 / Beers Criteria
cdus.entry_criteria: Neuropathic pain or depression in male patient with severe BPH (IPSS > 19)
mandated_actions: Select non-anticholinergic neuropathic agents (e.g. renally adjusted Pregabalin or Duloxetine)
negative_boundaries: 🛑 STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATE Tricyclic Antidepressants (Amitriptyline, Nortriptyline, Imipramine) in patients with severe lower urinary tract symptoms or severe BPH. Potent anticholinergic blockade inhibits detrusor muscle contraction, precipitating acute complete urinary retention requiring emergency catheterization.
cdus.verbatim_excerpt: Anticholinergic medications and tricyclic antidepressants (amitriptyline, nortriptyline) should be avoided in men with severe benign prostatic hyperplasia and lower urinary tract symptoms due to the risk of precipitating acute complete urinary retention.
danger_signs: Inability to void, severe lower abdominal distension and agony

cdus.source_guideline: KDIGO 2024 / FDA Dosing Guidance for Pregabalin and Gabapentin
cdus.entry_criteria: Neuropathic pain requiring gabapentinoids in patient with eGFR < 60 mL/min
mandated_actions: Reduce Pregabalin starting dose to 25-50mg BD (max maintenance 150mg/day) for eGFR 30-50 mL/min
Alternatively choose Duloxetine 30-60mg daily (safe down to eGFR 30 without renal dose reduction)
negative_boundaries: 🛑 DO NOT prescribe unadjusted full-dose Pregabalin (300-600mg/day) in eGFR <50 (causes severe CNS neurotoxicity, myoclonus, ataxia, falls).
cdus.verbatim_excerpt: Pregabalin and Gabapentin are cleared almost exclusively by renal excretion. In patients with eGFR 30-50 mL/min, maximum daily doses must be reduced by 50% to prevent neurotoxicity, profound somnolence, and falls.

hazards.name: Fatal Status Asthmaticus / Life-Threatening Bronchospasm
hazards.description: Non-selective beta-2 blockade triggers immediate catastrophic airway constriction in reactive airway disease.

hazards.name: Hepatorenal Syndrome / Refractory Renal Shutdown
hazards.description: NSAID inhibition of renal prostaglandins halts glomerular perfusion in cirrhotic portal hypertension.

hazards.name: Metformin-Associated Lactic Acidosis (MALA)
hazards.description: Accumulation of metformin during reduced renal clearance leads to severe, frequently lethal metabolic acidosis.

hazards.name: Ischemic Stroke or Myocardial Infarction from Vasospasm
hazards.description: 5-HT1B/1D vasoconstriction in uncontrolled severe hypertension triggers acute coronary occlusive spasm or ischemic stroke.

hazards.name: Irreversible Parkinsonian Motor Collapse / Bulbar Freezing
hazards.description: Dopamine D2 antagonism produces acute, potentially fatal motor freezing, rigidity, and loss of airway protection.

hazards.name: Catastrophic Hypoglycemic Coma and Fall-Induced Trauma
hazards.description: Delayed renal clearance of long-acting sulfonylureas in frail elderly causes refractory, prolonged hypoglycemia and fatal falls.

hazards.name: Catastrophic Upper Gastrointestinal Hemorrhage
hazards.description: Synergistic gastric mucosal ulceration from concurrent NSAID + oral anticoagulation increases fatal rebleeding by 4-6x.

hazards.name: Acute Complete Urinary Retention & Obstructive Uropathy
hazards.description: Potent anticholinergic blockade inhibits detrusor muscle contraction in severe bladder outlet obstruction, requiring emergency catheterization.

hazards.name: Acute-on-Chronic Kidney Injury
hazards.description: Hemodynamic reduction in glomerular filtration rate precipitated by nephrotoxic insults.

hazards.name: Severe Hyperkalemia (K+ >= 5.5 mmol/L)
hazards.description: Impaired potassium excretion from concurrent RAAS blockade and renal insufficiency carrying risk of cardiac arrest.

hazards.name: Fatal Hyperkalemic Arrhythmia / Asystole
hazards.description: Precipitous rise in serum potassium causing peaked T waves, conduction block, and fatal asystole.

hazards.name: Acute Precipitated Hepatic Encephalopathy
hazards.description: Sedative opioids depress respiration, prolong intestinal transit, and cross the blood-brain barrier in portal shunting.

hazards.name: Severe Gabapentinoid Myoclonus, Ataxia & Sedation
hazards.description: Drug accumulation from 100% renal elimination in reduced GFR causes severe myoclonus, encephalopathy, and falls.

hazards.name: Dose-Dependent Hepatotoxicity in Impaired Glutathione Reserves
hazards.description: Doses exceeding 2.0g/24h in cirrhosis exhaust depleted hepatic glutathione, producing toxic NAPQI accumulation.

hazards.name: Acute Heart Failure Decompensation & Sodium Retention
hazards.description: NSAID-induced prostaglandin inhibition promotes renal sodium and water retention, blunting loop diuretic efficacy.
